title: A parenthesis
logline: Wednesday. Julian introduces himself. The strip draws him as it always has: a pleasant shape, a neutral face, a linen shirt. He is kind. That's the hardest thing the strip has ever had to draw, and it draws it fair.

panels.composition: The pavilion's lawn. JULIAN, a pleasant shape in linen, hand out. WOOD, the suit, the sketchbook under his arm. CHLOE a step behind, watching both.

balloons.text: Arthur. Finally. She's — I've heard a great deal.
Woody. She said you'd say that.

image.prompt: razor-sharp brush and ink with pristine architectural perspective, blinding clear summer light in soft cerulean and pale linen watercolor, a pleasant indistinct man in a linen shirt offering his hand to a thin man in a dark suit on a bright lawn while a woman watches a step behind
image.notes: Julian: neutral, kind, deliberately unmemorable. The strip's fairness is the point. He says 'Arthur' once.

panels.composition: The handshake. Julian's hand: normal. Wood's: ink on the fingers.

image.prompt: razor-sharp brush and ink with pristine architectural perspective, blinding clear summer light in soft cerulean and pale linen watercolor, close-up of a handshake between a clean hand and a hand with ink stains on the fingers

balloons.text: The dog. The one at the top of the stairs — the March Sunday. I read it in the office and had to go for a walk.
All of them. I'm — sorry. I'm getting ahead.

image.prompt: razor-sharp brush and ink with pristine architectural perspective, blinding clear summer light in soft cerulean and pale linen watercolor, a pleasant man speaking earnestly to a thin man who is caught off guard
image.notes: Julian names dw_2014-03-16 (the dog at the top of the steps). He has read all of it, before Chloe says so in 2024.

panels.composition: Julian called away by a caterer. Wood and Chloe. Chloe looking at Wood's face, checking it.

image.prompt: razor-sharp brush and ink with pristine architectural perspective, blinding clear summer light in soft cerulean and pale linen watercolor, a woman checking a thin man's face on a lawn as a pleasant man walks away toward a caterer

art.line: razor-sharp, confident brush and ink; pristine perspective; crisp silhouettes; zero crosshatch in close-ups
art.palette: dailies: black ink, one spot tone at most. Sundays: wet-on-wet — gray-green moss, fog, rusted tin, bruised dusk
art.paper: bristol for dailies; 140 lb Arches cold-press for Sundays

notes: 'He's kind.' 'I was hoping for worse.' Drawn fair.
